024/**
025 * The configuration of a RainbowGum. In some other logging implementations this is called
026 * "context".
027 */
028public sealed interface LogConfig extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
029
030        /**
031         * String key value properties.
032         * @return properties.
033         */
034        @Override
035        public LogProperties properties();
036
037        /**
038         * Level resolver for resolving levels from logger names.
039         * @return level resolver.
040         */
041        public LevelConfig levelResolver();
042
043        /**
044         * Output provider that uses URI to find output.
045         * @return output provider.
046         */
047        public LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry();
048
049        /**
050         * Provides encoders by URI scheme.
051         * @return encoder registry.
052         */
053        public LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry();
054
055        /**
056         * Provides publishers by URI scheme.
057         * @return changePublisher registry.
058         */
059        public LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry();
060
061        /**
062         * Creates a builder for making LogConfig.
063         * @return builder.
064         */
065        public static Builder builder() {
066                return new Builder();
067        }
068
069        /**
070         * An event changePublisher to publish configuration changes.
071         * @return changePublisher.
072         */
073        public ChangePublisher changePublisher();
074
075        /**
076         * Service registry are custom services needed by plugins particularly during the
077         * initialization process.
078         * @return registry.
079         */
080        public ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry();
081
082        /**
083         * Alerts about problems with the logging system itself (as opposed to application
084         * logging routed through the {@link LogRouter}).
085         * @return alerts.
086         */
087        public LogAlerts alerts();
088
089        /**
090         * Metrics about the logging system itself (as opposed to application logging routed
091         * through the {@link LogRouter}).
092         * @return metrics.
093         */
094        public LogMetrics metrics();
095
096        /**
097         * Mixin for config support.
098         */
099        interface ConfigSupport extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
100
101                /**
102                 * Provides config.
103                 * @return config.
104                 */
105                public LogConfig config();
106
107                @Override
108                default LogProperties properties() {
109                        return config().properties();
110                }
111
112        }
113
114        /**
115         * Config Change Publisher. By default this is enabled with
116         * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY} set to <code>true</code>, which then
117         * gates two independent, per-logger-name properties:
118         * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX} + {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name,
119         * set to a list of {@link ChangeType} or <code>true</code>/<code>false</code> to
120         * enable or disable all changes, and {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX} +
121         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name, set to a {@link CallerType} (or
122         * <code>true</code>/<code>false</code>) to control caller info. The two are resolved
123         * independently - one does not imply or override the other, even for overlapping
124         * logger name prefixes.
125         */
126        interface ChangePublisher {
127
128                /**
129                 * Subscribe to changes.
130                 * @param consumer consumer.
131                 */
132                public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer);
133
134                /**
135                 * Publish that there has been changes.
136                 */
137                public void publish();
138
139                /**
140                 * Test to see if <strong>any</strong> changes are enabled for a logger - either
141                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} is non-empty or {@link #callerType(String)} is
142                 * not {@link CallerType#NONE}.
143                 * @param loggerName logger name.
144                 * @return true if enabled.
145                 */
146                public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName);
147
148                /**
149                 * Returns what the logger is allowed to change.
150                 * @param loggerName logger name.
151                 * @return which things are allowed to change in the logger
152                 */
153                public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName);
154
155                /**
156                 * The caller info level for a logger, resolved from
157                 * {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX}, independently of
158                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} /{@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX}. Unlike
159                 * {@link ChangeType#LEVEL}, which is genuinely re-evaluated on every
160                 * {@link #publish()}, this is resolved once when a logger is first created and
161                 * never revisited afterward - it reflects a static per-logger capability, not
162                 * something that changes at runtime.
163                 * @param loggerName logger name.
164                 * @return caller type, {@link CallerType#NONE} if not configured.
165                 */
166                public CallerType callerType(String loggerName);
167
168                /**
169                 * Whether caller info should be computed for a logger at all, regardless of which
170                 * non-{@link CallerType#NONE} level.
171                 * @param loggerName logger name.
172                 * @return true if caller info is enabled for this logger.
173                 */
174                default boolean callerInfoEnabled(String loggerName) {
175                        return callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
176                }
177
178                /**
179                 * Changing type options.
180                 */
181                public enum ChangeType {
182
183                        /**
184                         * The logger is allowed to change levels.
185                         */
186                        LEVEL;
187
188                        static Set<ChangeType> parse(List<String> value) {
189                                if (value.isEmpty()) {
190                                        return Set.of();
191                                }
192                                var s = EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
193                                for (var v : value) {
194                                        if (v.equalsIgnoreCase("true")) {
195                                                return EnumSet.allOf(ChangeType.class);
196                                        }
197                                        if (v.equalsIgnoreCase("false")) {
198                                                return EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
199                                        }
200                                        s.add(ChangeType.parse(v));
201                                }
202                                return s;
203                        }
204
205                        static ChangeType parse(String value) {
206                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
207                                return ChangeType.valueOf(v);
208                        }
209
210                }
211
212                /**
213                 * Caller info levels, resolved from {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX}.
214                 * {@link #BASIC} is the only level implemented today (a stack-walk down to the
215                 * calling class/method/line) - kept as an enum rather than a boolean so a future,
216                 * richer level (matching what some other logging frameworks gather from the
217                 * stack) can be added without a breaking property-format change.
218                 */
219                public enum CallerType {
220
221                        /**
222                         * Caller info is not computed.
223                         */
224                        NONE,
225                        /**
226                         * Caller info is computed as a single stack frame (class, method, line).
227                         */
228                        BASIC;
229
230                        static CallerType parse(String value) {
231                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
232                                return switch (v) {
233                                        case "TRUE" -> BASIC;
234                                        case "FALSE" -> NONE;
235                                        default -> CallerType.valueOf(v);
236                                };
237                        }
238
239                }
240
241        }
242
243        /**
244         * Builder for LogConfig.
245         * <p>
246         * <strong>NOTE:</strong> The service loader is not used by default with this builder.
247         * If the automatic discovery of components is desired call
248         * {@link #serviceLoader(ServiceLoader)}.
249         */
250        public static final class Builder extends LevelResolver.AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
251
252                private @Nullable ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry;
253
254                private @Nullable LogProperties logProperties;
255
256                private @Nullable ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader;
257
258                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator> configurators = new ArrayList<>();
259
260                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider> propertiesProviders = new ArrayList<>();
261
262                /**
263                 * Default constructor
264                 */
265                private Builder() {
266                }
267
268                /**
269                 * Sets log properties
270                 * @param logProperties log properties.
271                 * @return this.
272                 */
273                public Builder properties(LogProperties logProperties) {
274                        this.logProperties = logProperties;
275                        return this;
276                }
277
278                /**
279                 * Sets service registry
280                 * @param serviceRegistry service registry.
281                 * @return this.
282                 */
283                public Builder serviceRegistry(ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry) {
284                        this.serviceRegistry = serviceRegistry;
285                        return this;
286                }
287
288                /**
289                 * Add to configure LogConfig and ServiceRegistry.
290                 * @param configurator will run on build.
291                 * @return this.
292                 */
293                public Builder configurator(RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator configurator) {
294                        configurators.add(configurator);
295                        return this;
296                }
297
298                /**
299                 * Add properties.
300                 * @param propertiesProvider will run on build.
301                 * @return this.
302                 */
303                public Builder propertiesProvider(RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider propertiesProvider) {
304                        propertiesProviders.add(propertiesProvider);
305                        return this;
306                }
307
308                /**
309                 * Sets the service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
310                 * @param serviceLoader loader to use for missing components.
311                 * @return this.
312                 */
313                public Builder serviceLoader(ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader) {
314                        this.serviceLoader = serviceLoader;
315                        return this;
316                }
317
318                /**
319                 * Sets a default service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
320                 * This call will just call the {@link ServiceLoader} without providing a class
321                 * loader.
322                 * @return this.
323                 */
324                public Builder serviceLoader() {
325                        return this.serviceLoader(ServiceLoader.load(RainbowGumServiceProvider.class));
326                }
327
328                /**
329                 * Configures the builder with a function for ergonomics.
330                 * @param consumer passed the builder.
331                 * @return this.
332                 */
333                public Builder with(Consumer<? super Builder> consumer) {
334                        consumer.accept(this);
335                        return this;
336                }
337
338                /**
339                 * Builds LogConfig which will use the {@link ServiceLoader} if set to load
340                 * missing components and if not set will use static defaults.
341                 * @return log config
342                 */
343                public LogConfig build() {
344                        ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry = this.serviceRegistry;
345                        LogProperties logProperties = this.logProperties;
346
347                        var serviceLoader = this.serviceLoader;
348                        var configurators = this.configurators;
349                        if (serviceRegistry == null) {
350                                serviceRegistry = ServiceRegistry.of();
351                        }
352                        if (logProperties == null) {
353                                List<LogProperties> props = new ArrayList<>();
354                                for (var pp : propertiesProviders) {
355                                        props.addAll(pp.provideProperties(serviceRegistry));
356                                }
357                                if (props.isEmpty() && serviceLoader != null) {
358                                        props.addAll(provideProperties(serviceRegistry, serviceLoader));
359                                }
360                                logProperties = LogProperties.of(props, LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
361
362                        }
363                        /*
364                         * Built before DefaultLogConfig itself (rather than left for
365                         * DefaultLogConfig's constructor to create, as before) specifically so
366                         * buildGlobalResolver below can hand LogAlerts to the global level resolver's
367                         * alerting wrapper - the global resolver is built before a full LogConfig
368                         * exists to pull config.alerts() from, so alerts (and metrics, via alerts'
369                         * own listener wiring) are constructed directly here instead. Capacity and
370                         * logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction both come from logProperties as
371                         * already resolved above - before any configurator runs, the same as
372                         * everything else built directly in this method - see
373                         * DefaultLogAlerts.of(...) for how the two are validated together.
374                         */
375                        LogAlerts alerts = DefaultLogAlerts.of(logProperties);
376                        LogMetrics metrics = new DefaultLogMetrics();
377                        var levelResolver = this.buildGlobalResolver(logProperties, alerts);
378                        var config = new DefaultLogConfig(serviceRegistry, logProperties, levelResolver, alerts, metrics);
379                        if (serviceLoader != null) {
380                                configurators = new ArrayList<>(configurators);
381                                findProviders(serviceLoader, Configurator.class).forEach(configurators::add);
382                        }
383                        if (!configurators.isEmpty()) {
384                                /*
385                                 * TODO two-pass config: configurators run after config (and therefore the
386                                 * global level resolver above) already exists, so a configurator that
387                                 * contributes additional property sources or otherwise changes what the
388                                 * level resolver should have seen is invisible to it - the resolver was
389                                 * already built from logProperties as it stood before any configurator
390                                 * ran. A more correct design would run configurators first, then rebuild
391                                 * whatever is purely derived from properties (starting with the level
392                                 * resolver) a second time against the now-fully-configured LogConfig. Not
393                                 * done here - see todo.md.
394                                 */
395                                RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator.runConfigurators(configurators.stream(), config);
396                        }
397                        /*
398                         * Deliberately last: alerts already resolved LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction
399                         * at construction above, but only now, once configurators have had their
400                         * chance to record alerts and/or register a real Listener, does "should I
401                         * report/refuse to start" actually mean anything - by construction nothing
402                         * has had a chance to register one before this point.
403                         */
404                        alerts.start(config);
405                        return config;
406                }
407
408                LevelConfig buildGlobalResolver(LogProperties logProperties, LogAlerts alerts) {
409                        LevelConfig levelResolver = LevelConfig
410                                .of(List.of(ConfigLevelResolver.of(logProperties), GroupLevelResolver.of(logProperties)));
411                        var config = buildLevelConfigOrNull();
412                        if (config != null) {
413                                levelResolver = LevelConfig.of(List.<LevelConfig>of(config, levelResolver));
414                        }
415                        return new AlertingLevelConfig(levelResolver, alerts);
416                }
417
418                private static List<LogProperties> provideProperties(ServiceRegistry registry,
419                                ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> loader) {
420                        List<LogProperties> props = findProviders(loader, PropertiesProvider.class)
421                                .flatMap(s -> s.provideProperties(registry).stream())
422                                .toList();
423                        return props;
424                }
425
426                @Override
427                protected Builder self() {
428                        return this;
429                }
430
431        }
432
433}
434
435abstract class AbstractChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
436
437        /*
438         * TODO Ideally this would be a concurrent weak hashmap. The reasoning is we may want
439         * a configuration where SLF4J loggers are not stored in concurrent hash map but some
440         * sort of GC friendly cache or not cached at all. If they subscribe to changes the
441         * loggers will never be GCed.
442         *
443         * Consequently the functional Consumer interface might not be the best choice.
444         */
445        private final Collection<Consumer<? super LogConfig>> consumers = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<Consumer<? super LogConfig>>();
446
447        /*
448         * Same shape as LevelResolver.java's CachedLevelResolver: allowedChanges(name) is
449         * only ever called once per never-before-seen logger name (RainbowGumLoggerFactory
450         * caches the resulting Logger forever afterward), so a ConcurrentHashMap here matches
451         * the exact call pattern that made a ConcurrentHashMap the right tradeoff there too.
452         */
453        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, Set<ChangeType>> changesCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
454
455        /*
456         * Sibling to changesCache, not folded into it - CallerType is resolved from its own
457         * logging.caller.<name> property, independent of logging.change.<name>, so it gets
458         * its own map rather than a combined per-name struct (one map per concern).
459         */
460        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, CallerType> callerTypeCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
461
462        protected abstract LogConfig reload();
463
464        protected abstract LogConfig config();
465
466        @Override
467        public void publish() {
468                changesCache.clear();
469                callerTypeCache.clear();
470                LogConfig config = reload();
471                for (var c : consumers) {
472                        c.accept(config);
473                }
474        }
475
476        @Override
477        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
478                consumers.add(consumer);
479        }
480
481        @Override
482        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
483                return !allowedChanges(loggerName).isEmpty() || callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
484        }
485
486        @Override
487        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
488                return changesCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
489                        /*
490                         * findOrNull walks the logger-name hierarchy (closest match wins, see its own
491                         * javadoc) trying each candidate key in turn - per candidate, resolve it as a
492                         * LogProperty and only return null (telling findOrNull to keep walking up)
493                         * when the key is genuinely Missing there. A present-but-malformed value is a
494                         * Result.Error, not a Missing - it must stop the walk right there rather than
495                         * silently falling through to a less specific ancestor's value.
496                         */
497                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> result = config().properties()
498                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CHANGE_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
499                                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofList().map(ChangeType::parse);
500                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
501                                });
502                        if (result == null) {
503                                return Set.of();
504                        }
505                        try {
506                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
507                        }
508                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
509                                /*
510                                 * A malformed logging.change.<name> value must not be able to break
511                                 * logging itself. ConcurrentHashMap#computeIfAbsent leaves nothing cached
512                                 * when the mapping function throws, so without catching this a bad
513                                 * property would re-parse and re-alert on every single allowedChanges(n)
514                                 * call for this logger name, not just once - same amplification risk
515                                 * CachedLevelResolver guards against for level properties. Fall back to
516                                 * "nothing allowed to change" and alert exactly once per logger name
517                                 * instead, since the fallback value is itself cached above just like a
518                                 * successful parse would be. validateNow's own Missing = failure
519                                 * semantics are moot here - the lambda above never returns a Missing
520                                 * result to it in the first place.
521                                 */
522                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
523                                return Set.of();
524                        }
525                });
526        }
527
528        @Override
529        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
530                return callerTypeCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
531                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> result = config().properties()
532                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CALLER_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
533                                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofString().map(CallerType::parse);
534                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
535                                });
536                        if (result == null) {
537                                return CallerType.NONE;
538                        }
539                        try {
540                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
541                        }
542                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
543                                /*
544                                 * Same reasoning as allowedChanges()'s catch above: a malformed (or
545                                 * pre-split, e.g. the old "caller" token that used to live in
546                                 * logging.change.<name>) logging.caller.<name> value alerts once and
547                                 * falls back to CallerType.NONE, cached, rather than re-parsing and
548                                 * re-alerting on every call.
549                                 */
550                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
551                                return CallerType.NONE;
552                        }
553                });
554        }
555
556}
557
558enum IgnoreChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
559
560        INSTANT;
561
562        @Override
563        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
564        }
565
566        @Override
567        public void publish() {
568
569        }
570
571        @Override
572        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
573                return false;
574        }
575
576        @Override
577        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
578                return Set.of();
579        }
580
581        @Override
582        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
583                return CallerType.NONE;
584        }
585
586}
587
588final class DefaultLogConfig implements LogConfig {
589
590        private final ServiceRegistry registry;
591
592        private final LogProperties properties;
593
594        private final LevelConfig levelResolver;
595
596        private final ChangePublisher changePublisher;
597
598        private final LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry;
599
600        private final LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry;
601
602        private final LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry;
603
604        private final LogAlerts alerts;
605
606        private final LogMetrics metrics;
607
608        DefaultLogConfig(ServiceRegistry registry, LogProperties properties, LevelConfig levelResolver, LogAlerts alerts,
609                        LogMetrics metrics) {
610                super();
611                this.registry = registry;
612                this.properties = properties;
613                this.levelResolver = levelResolver;
614                this.alerts = alerts;
615                this.metrics = metrics;
616                boolean changeable = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY)
617                        .ofBoolean()
618                        .or(false)
619                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
620                this.changePublisher = changeable ? new DefaultChangePublisher() : IgnoreChangePublisher.INSTANT;
621                applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(properties);
622                applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(properties);
623                this.outputRegistry = DefaultOutputRegistry.of(registry);
624                this.encoderRegistry = DefaultEncoderRegistry.of();
625                this.publisherRegistry = DefaultPublisherRegistry.of();
626                /*
627                 * addInternalListener, not addListener: a passive in-process counter nobody has
628                 * wired an exporter to does not count as "someone is watching" for
629                 * LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction's purposes - see DefaultLogAlerts's own
630                 * comment on hasExternalListener. alerts is always a DefaultLogAlerts; LogAlerts
631                 * is sealed to permit only that one implementation.
632                 */
633                ((DefaultLogAlerts) this.alerts).addInternalListener(event -> this.metrics.errorCounter(event.loggerName(), 1));
634        }
635
636        /*
637         * Deliberately mutates process-wide static state (AbstractLogAppender's field) rather
638         * than per-instance state - LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY is
639         * a global guarantee by design (see its javadoc), not a per-LogConfig setting.
640         * Last-writer-wins if multiple RainbowGum instances with different values coexist in
641         * one JVM - an accepted tradeoff for a property whose whole point is a process-wide
642         * guarantee independent of any single instance's configuration.
643         */
644        private static void applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(LogProperties properties) {
645                AbstractLogAppender.forceReentrantLockAppenders = properties
646                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY)
647                        .ofBoolean()
648                        .or(false)
649                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
650        }
651
652        /*
653         * An enum (TRUE/FALSE) rather than .ofBoolean() deliberately, unlike its sibling just
654         * above - a typo'd value here (e.g. "yse") fails loudly through the existing
655         * Property/Result machinery instead of silently resolving to "not disabled", which is
656         * the wrong failure mode for a property whose whole point is a hard, otherwise
657         * easy-to-silently-miss guarantee.
658         */
659        private enum ThreadLocalDisabled {
660
661                TRUE, FALSE;
662
663                static ThreadLocalDisabled parse(String value) {
664                        return ThreadLocalDisabled.valueOf(value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
665                }
666
667        }
668
669        /*
670         * Same last-writer-wins/process-wide-guarantee tradeoff as
671         * applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty just above - see that method's comment.
672         * rainbowgum-slf4j independently reads this same property key at its own SLF4J
673         * provider initialize() touchpoint to decide whether to disable MDC too - see
674         * LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY's javadoc for why that is two
675         * independent readers rather than one shared flag.
676         */
677        private static void applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(LogProperties properties) {
678                AbstractLogAppender.forceNoThreadLocalAppenders = properties
679                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY)
680                        .ofString()
681                        .map(ThreadLocalDisabled::parse)
682                        .or(ThreadLocalDisabled.FALSE)
683                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class) == ThreadLocalDisabled.TRUE;
684        }
685
686        class DefaultChangePublisher extends AbstractChangePublisher {
687
688                @Override
689                protected LogConfig config() {
690                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
691                }
692
693                @Override
694                protected LogConfig reload() {
695                        levelResolver.clear();
696                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;
697                }
698
699        }
700
701        @Override
702        public LogProperties properties() {
703                return properties;
704        }
705
706        @Override
707        public LevelConfig levelResolver() {
708                return this.levelResolver;
709        }
710
711        @Override
712        public ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry() {
713                return this.registry;
714        }
715
716        @Override
717        public ChangePublisher changePublisher() {
718                return this.changePublisher;
719        }
720
721        @Override
722        public LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry() {
723                return this.outputRegistry;
724        }
725
726        @Override
727        public LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry() {
728                return this.encoderRegistry;
729        }
730
731        @Override
732        public LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry() {
733                return this.publisherRegistry;
734        }
735
736        @Override
737        public LogAlerts alerts() {
738                return this.alerts;
739        }
740
